title: On a phone, long button words run past the screen edge on the Delete requests page
what: HQ buttons never break their words onto a second line. On a phone the delete request steps are buttons with long words, such as 'I called the gym's own number and the owner confirmed' and 'I reminded them to download their data first', and the button 'Write it down for' carries the gym's full name. At 320 to 390 px wide these buttons are wider than the screen, so the words are pushed past the edge and the page slides sideways, on the one page where a step must not be missed.
expected: Every button fits the phone width: long words break onto a second line, or the button is shorter.
how_often: every time a delete request is open on a phone
fix_line: Let button words wrap on phones, or shorten the step buttons.

title: Messages says a message reaches the gyms' bell within a minute; an open admin app looks only every 15 minutes
what: The Messages page says a message shows in the bell of every gym's admin app within a minute. An admin app that is already open asks for new messages only every 15 minutes, and the answer can also sit a minute in the browser. So a gym at its desk can wait up to about 16 minutes to see it.
expected: The words say how long it really takes (up to about a quarter of an hour, or as soon as the admin app is opened), or the admin app asks more often.
fix_line: Change the words to 'within about 15 minutes, or when the admin app is opened'.

title: Pausing a gym says members keep their app, but members cannot check in or order while it is paused
what: Before pausing, HQ says staff can still look and download and 'Members keep their app'. A paused gym refuses every new record: check-ins, receipts, shop orders and gym messages are all stopped by the database. Members can open the app, but their own check-in and shop orders fail. The words make a pause sound harmless to members when it is not.
expected: The pause words say plainly what members lose: they can open the app but cannot check in or order until the gym is un-paused.
fix_line: Add to the pause words that members cannot check in or order while the gym is paused.

title: The read log warning on Needs you looks like a link but opens the same page
what: When the read log stops working or its key is about to end, Needs you shows a red or yellow card with an arrow, like every other line. Tapping it opens Needs you again, the page you are already on. Nothing tells you where to go to fix it.
expected: A card with an arrow opens the place where the problem is fixed, or it has no arrow and says the next step in its words.
how_often: whenever the read log has a problem
fix_line: Drop the arrow on these lines, or point them to the System page with the fix steps.

title: Show older on the Log does nothing when it fails
what: Every other HQ button shows a message when something goes wrong. Show older on the Log page has no place for one: if the sign-in has run out or the server does not answer, the button greys for a moment and then nothing happens, with the reason only in the hidden browser console.
expected: A failed Show older says why next to the button, like the other buttons.
fix_line: Give Show older a message box like the other buttons.

title: The Log says it holds every look at a gym, but looks made straight in the database are not in it
what: The Log page says it shows everything done in HQ and every look at a gym. Looks made with the database's own login (its table editor, its query page, direct tools) are recorded in a separate list kept 2 years, and the database even has a ready way for HQ to read that list. HQ never asks for it, so those looks never show in HQ.
expected: Either HQ shows the direct database looks (on the Log or its own page), or the Log words say they are kept elsewhere.
fix_line: Show the direct database looks in HQ, or change the Log words.

title: HQ messages name database updates by number
what: When a tool is not ready, HQ says things like 'Payments need the database update 0060' or 'its web database update (0015) is applied'. The numbers mean nothing to the reader and do not say which tool is waiting or what to do.
expected: The words name the tool that waits and the next step in plain words, with no code numbers.
how_often: while a tool waits for its update
fix_line: Replace the numbers with the tool's name and 'waiting for your yes'.

title: A message button can point to an admin app page that does not exist
what: The Messages page asks for the page the button opens, like /plans or /settings. HQ accepts any address that looks like a page name and does not check it is a real admin app page. One typo sends every gym a button that does not open what it names.
expected: HQ offers a pick-list of real admin app pages, or refuses an address that is not one.
fix_line: Give the button a pick-list of real admin app pages.

title: HQ's install card calls it the owner panel, the name people give the gyms' admin app
what: When HQ is installed on a phone or computer, its description reads 'The MettleUp owner panel.' Everywhere else the gym owners' tool is the admin app and this one is HQ, so the install card mixes the two names.
expected: One name for each: HQ is MettleUp's own control room, the admin app is the gym owner's.
fix_line: Describe HQ as MettleUp's own control room.
